_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for MSFT retrospectives (retro/build_msft.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2002); every Microsoft earnings 8-K of the period was accepted after the close, with the 10-Q minutes apart. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest fiscal-year EPS range for the current year (its midpoint), the latest next-quarter revenue range (as growth on the year-ago quarter's revenue from its own filing), and the latest declared dividend. Microsoft's fiscal year ends on June 30. Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, per share as published (the February 2003 two-for-one split restates the years published before it: 'eps_published', 'shares_published'), and a company figure excluding one-offs only replaces GAAP EPS (the history's 'normalization' says which). A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the raw figures of its release or the 10-Q filed with it ('raw'; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago balance sheet comes from the year-ago quarter's own 10-Q or release, unearned revenue is short- plus long-term, and a comparable operating income replaces GAAP only when the release gives it for both quarters and it excludes only one-offs; lc_pct (from the Q2 FY09 print, the first without a next-quarter guide) is the revenue growth the release states less the currency effect the release or the 10-Q filed with it states, the reported growth where none is stated; a total effect stated only in dollars ('fx_impact_m' in 'raw', favorable positive; Q1 and Q2 FY12) is taken off the quarter's revenue, (revenue - effect) / year-ago revenue - 1, rounded half up to a whole percent (the builder re-derives it), and a segment's effect alone is not the quarter's; a constant-currency revenue growth the release labels non-GAAP is the reported revenue's only where the same table's non-GAAP revenue is the reported revenue (2018-2020, whose adjustments are tax items and restructuring below revenue; not 2015-2017, whose non-GAAP revenue removes the Windows 10 deferrals). From the Q2 FY09 release Microsoft gives no revenue or EPS guide in numbers: that release withdraws the fiscal 2009 guide ('withdrawn' voids every earlier guide for its year), and the fiscal 2009-2014 operating expense ranges ('opex_guide_usd_b') are display only; from the Q1 FY14 release Microsoft gives guidance only on its conference call, which is not a filing, so nothing is entered. A Q4 print's fiscal-year actuals may restate an earlier year's EPS to a company figure excluding only one-offs first published in that release ('restates' in 'fy_actual'), until the next 10-K vintage carries it. From the Q1 FY16 release the company's non-GAAP figures also remove the Windows 10 revenue deferrals, which are revenue recognition, not one-offs: GAAP stands for those years and prints. A filing that re-presents earlier years on a new accounting basis is a vintage of its own (the 8-K of 2017-08-03: FY2016-FY2017 under the new revenue and lease standards, earlier years as published); it keeps the latest 10-K's wording and CLOUD event ('text_published' gives that 10-K's date). A print whose year-ago balance sheet no filing gives on the print's own basis has unearned revenue not comparable ('unearned_prior_m' null, read as not reported: Q1 FY18 under the new standards); its receivables keep the year-ago balance as published, with the restatement's size in the note. Events: each 10-K's cloud risk factor (kind cloud_company_acknowledged, id = the 10-K's source), used only from CLOUD's live date in retro/taxonomy_eras.json; from the FY2023 10-K, the first Microsoft filing that names AI as a competitive market and competitors' open source AI models, its AI wording too (kind genai_company_acknowledged, the same id; GENAI is live from 2022-11-30). From the FY2021 10-K Item 6 is reserved, so a vintage takes the three years of its income statements and each earlier year from the latest 10-K that reports it. The 8-K of 2022-06-02 restates the fourth quarter of fiscal 2022 in numbers after currency moves (revenue, operating income and EPS ranges the company calculated from its segment guidance): a next-quarter guide in a filing ('q_guide'). Guides start with the Q4 FY07 release (the Q3 FY07 release's preliminary fiscal 2008 range is superseded before any built date). rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'MSFT'): the ten annual values FY1998-FY2007 (the decade of the FY2007 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04). Revenue growth from the five-year summary of the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years; the margins from the income statements of the latest 10-K that reports both years; unearned revenue (short- and long-term) and the receivables gap within each year's own 10-K (its two balance sheets and its income statement). A company figure excluding one-offs replaces the reported one where it was published for both years on the same basis: FY2006 and FY2007 operating income as adjusted ($17,581M and $19,735M, Q4 FY07 release). Everything else as reported, seams included (the FY1999 revenue-recognition restatement of FY1997-FY1998 revenue and cost of revenue, the SFAS 123 restatement of FY2002-FY2003, reclassifications between 10-Ks).
